name: Android Auto Backup and restore
plain: Android copies up to 25 MB of app data to Google Drive about once a day and restores it at the next install.
meaning: A reinstall or new phone can bring old app data back, including identifiers the developer stored. Android 16 QPR2 adds transfer of some data to iOS.

android.persistence: Up to 25 MB per app in Google Drive; runs about once every 24 h on idle, charging, unmetered network
android.revocation: Turn off in Settings or exclude paths
android.store_policy: Play: sensitive data should be excluded
android.note: 25 MB limit per app; backup about every 24 h; restore runs at install before first launch; backup deleted after 57 days of device inactivity (unverified)

ios.note: iOS equivalent is iCloud Backup (whole container); see mob.os.icloud-backup-kvs

limits.headline: Can save up to 25 MB of app data to your Google account daily
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when Android backup is on and the phone is idle
can: Back up app settings and data, up to 25 MB, roughly every 24 hours
Restore that data when you reinstall or set up a new phone
Restore before the first launch of the app
cannot: Back up when you turned off Settings, Google, Backup
Keep backups for a phone you stopped using; they are deleted after 57 days
Do this on iPhone, which uses iCloud Backup instead
limits.reach_label: A daily copy of app data
limits.differs: Android has Auto Backup with a 25 MB cap. iPhone backs up the whole app folder with iCloud Backup.

story.what_it_is: Android quietly copies up to 25 MB of app data to Google Drive and restores it on reinstall.

marketing.name: Auto Backup for apps
marketing.pitch: Google describes Auto Backup as a way for apps to save data to Drive so it returns after a reinstall or a new phone.

story.for_you: You get a new phone and your app settings and progress are already there. You never press backup. The same thing happens after a reinstall.
story.for_makers: Makers get restores for free. The downside is that stored identifiers can also return, so one person can look like the same user across reinstalls.

use_cases.example: A new phone loads your saved game and settings.
A notes app restores local notes.
A workout app brings back your plan.
An ad SDK that saved an ID in app storage finds the same ID after a reinstall.
A bank app must make sure old tokens are not restored by a backup.
A team sees a returning device with the same ID and links it to the old user.
A chat app restores settings but asks you to sign in again.

story.android_note: About 25 MB per app, once about every 24 hours, restored at install before first launch.
story.ios_note: iOS uses iCloud Backup of the whole app container instead.

technical_bounds: Excluded when the app opts out or user disables backup

history.change: Cross platform data transfer to iOS announced
